title: Adaptive Token-Length Tuner with Kernel Handoff and Prefill Prioritization
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: High token padding and suboptimal kernel selection on heterogeneous requests increase per-token cost and tail latency. Goal: Implement an adaptive token-length tuner that groups requests by effective token-duration (not just raw seqlen), produces kernel affinity hints, and adjusts prefill vs decode scheduling priorities to minimize wasted compute and reduce worst-case tail latency. Approach: 1) Estimate "effective length" using prefix token reuse, attention sparsity signals, and per-customer decode patterns; 2) Map length buckets to preferred kernel/quantization profiles (kernel handoff table) and prefill priority classes; 3) Integrate with scheduler to shift short-prefill/low-attention requests earlier and allow long-decode requests to be coalesced with tolerant latency budgets. Deliverables: design doc, scheduler patch, kernel-handoff table config, e2e microbench harness, perf dashboard tiles. Success metrics: 10-20% reduction in padded token volume, 5-15% cost/unit reduction on mixed workloads, 95th percentile latency improvement by 10% on targeted tenants. Risks: misclassification causing increased latency for priority traffic; complexity in maintaining kernel affinity across model variants. Rollout: staged feature flag gated by canary traffic and per-tenant opt-in.
